questions.q: Why must you validate an LLM's JSON reply in your own code even if the prompt asked for a strict format?
options: Because the json module cannot parse model output
Because models always return prose
Because a prompt instruction is a request, not a guarantee, and bad output can corrupt your table
Because validation makes the model cheaper
questions.explain: Models can return code fences, missing fields, invented values, or chatty text. Validation is what protects downstream data.

questions.q: One canned reply was JSON wrapped in a markdown code fence. What did the validator in this lesson do with it?
options: Rejected it as invalid JSON
Crashed with a KeyError
Silently changed the category
Stripped the fence, parsed it, and accepted it
questions.explain: Stripping the code fence before parsing rescued that reply, a very common formatting quirk.

questions.q: A reply used the category "refund", which is not in the allowed list. What is the right handling?
options: Accept it, since a new category is probably fine
Reject it with a clear error, and retry or route to a human
Delete the category field
Convert it to an integer
questions.explain: Allowed-value checks catch invented labels. The error message can be fed back to the model for a retry.

questions.q: Why does the retry loop append the validation error to the prompt and cap the attempts?
options: The error tells the model what to fix, and the cap prevents endless, costly loops
The API refuses more than three prompts
It makes the JSON shorter
It hides the mistake from the user
questions.explain: Feeding back the error gives the model something concrete to correct, while a maximum number of tries bounds cost and time. Failures go to a human.

questions.q: How were the model outputs produced in this lesson's runnable code?
options: By a hosted API using a real key
By a local neural network trained in the lesson
By canned replies written by hand, including deliberately broken ones
By pydantic
questions.explain: No model was called. Hand-written good and bad replies let you test the validator and retry loop offline.
